questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the courses the university offered matched my profile/interests within biology.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would really recommend taking your time to choose the right country not by how nice it is but what it can offer you.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was fairly easy once I knew where to find it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not need any assistance and more or less figured it out myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I signed up to get offers on housing but ended up getting housing off campus which was offered and owned by the university so it was actually quite easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For me as an exchange student I really enjoyed living off campus as I lived closer to the city center so I would say depending on the person it all has pros and cons but I am happy that I got to live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be aware that not all universities can assure you that you will get housing which was the case for me. However I was lucky also because I signed up for housing early so I will definitely recommend doing that.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it would have been nice to have a document available with how it worked signing up for courses at my university and also how you could see if a course was a master og bachelor course as it did not say so in the course description.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
At my university they have 3 periods in one semester. The first period you choose two courses and it has to be a morning and an afternoon course and the same is for the second period. The last period you only have one course. 
We enrolled for courses through an app/website called OSIRIS which was very easy to do once you had figured out the courses you wished to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
We had a course catalog available and then I found some information about the morning and afternoon courses and how many courses you could take in each period. 
I do however think that the information could have been more easily accesable.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would say it was succesfull as I registret for all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you choose a morning and an afternoon course when having a period with two courses (it says in the course description if it is a morning or afternoon course). Also make sure you are aware if it is a period with one or two courses as I almost signed up for two courses in period 3 where they recommend only one as it is very intense in that period.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offered many different and interesting courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would personally say that the level of the courses was a lot higher than I expected as each period was very short and for me it was a bit too stressfull to have 5 exams divided into three exam period in one semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say it was similar in many ways although in many cases I felt like the expectations were higher in some cases especially when it came to the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sustainability and Resilience in History (RHI50806) - Period 1
Life History of Aquatic Organisms (AFI31306) - Period 1
Immunology and Thermoregulation (ADP20306) - Period 2
Wildlife Ecology and Conservation (WEC32806) - Period 2
Pyrogeography (SGL40306) - Period 3

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Pyrogeography as I fell like it is very underated. Fires become more and more a critical issue so the knowledge I gained in this course has been really useful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay a water cost with many others where I lived however it was not much.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The only thing that was a bit more expensive than expected was eating out however it was not more expensive than in Denmark but compared to everthing else being a bit cheaper eating out was not.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was surprised by the different opportunities they offered which was nice and a good way of being included in something.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different sports as well as clubs. Many including myself was an ESN member and they would often make different activities or even trips for example top October fest.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend being a member of the ESN as this is also a good way of getting to know fellow exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going and visiting some of the cities nearby where there is not as many tourists.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The dutch culture is not that different from the danish culture so I adjusted pretty fast.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open minded especially in the start. You might be tired and overwhelmed but still try and go socialise as it is very important in the start of your exchange.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the kindness towards exchanged students very much as I felt very welcomed in the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open minded, join social activities and do not be afraid of meeting knew people and I believe you will be welcomed and meet with kindness.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No that I can think of and that I have not already mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The things I learned about myself and other cultures that I would not have learned otherwise. Also concerning courses as some people had a very different way of thinking than I have experienced back in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being far from home and not really having any of the people back home who really knows you.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can definitely recommend studying abroad as you will get an experience of a lifetime.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
